card.name: Adverbs of timing before available
card.fires_on: Time adverbs such as continuously, instantly or yearly that come right after "are" or a noun phrase, and the "-term" in "short-term". They appear in label sentences about what must be available or what is done over time.

modes.label: Availability adverbs
modes.description: An adverb like continuously or instantly sits between "are" and "available" in a facilities requirement.
modes.example: setting where facilities and personnel for monitoring and resuscitation are<< continuously>>

modes.label: Short-term
modes.description: The "-term" part of "short-term" before trials or infusions.

modes.label: Other time or state words
modes.description: Words like current or yearly that modify an event or condition.
modes.example: Test all patients for evidence of<< current>> or prior HBV infection

card.plain: It fires on small timing words like "continuously" or "instantly" that come just before a word such as "available".
